_comment: Memory-type taxonomy cards. Based on the CoALA framing (Sumers et al. 2023) which remains the field's shared vocabulary. Edited by the nightly maintenance job.

types.label: in the context window
types.title: Working memory
types.body: Whatever is in the context window right now: the conversation, tool results, retrieved memories. It's the only memory the model can actually attend to - everything else exists to feed it. Finite, expensive, and degrades when overloaded (“context rot”).
types.example: In the scenario: the Friday-dinner request, plus whichever of m1–m5 retrieval just loaded.
types.policies: Written implicitly by running. Maintained by compaction: summarize-and-restart when the window fills.

types.label: what happened
types.title: Episodic memory
types.body: Records of specific events: conversations, actions taken, outcomes. High volume, individually low value - but the raw material every other kind is distilled from, and the only source of precedent (“like last time”).
types.example: m2 - “Booked Luna for Maya + Sam, Friday 19:00.” And m5, the breakup conversation.
types.policies: Written by automatic logging. Retrieved by recency or similarity. Maintained by summarization and TTL expiry - old episodes get compressed into semantic facts, then dropped.

types.label: what is true
types.title: Semantic memory
types.body: Distilled facts about the world, stripped of the episode that taught them: preferences, relationships, constraints. Small, dense, high value per token - and the kind that can silently become false.
types.example: m1 - “Maya is allergic to peanuts.” m3 - “Sam is Maya's partner” (true until Aug 18).
types.policies: Written by LLM extraction from episodes. Retrieved by subject/type filters or similarity. Maintained by contradiction resolution and supersession - the hardest maintenance job there is.

types.label: how to behave
types.title: Procedural memory
types.body: Skills, rules, and learned behaviour - including the system prompt itself. Not facts about the world but policies for acting in it. Usually loaded unconditionally rather than retrieved, because a rule you don't load is a rule you don't follow.
types.example: m4 - “Before booking any restaurant, check the menu for peanut dishes.” Learned from a near-miss.
types.policies: Written by deliberate promotion - a lesson has to earn its place. Maintained by review: stale rules cost adherence on every future task.
